open_questions: Read Simon Poole's chapter 'Speed King: Setting the Paice' (2025) in full: only its abstract was read; its nine Mark II intros may give transcriptions to check these patterns against.

Lazy, Pictures of Home, Child in Time and Space Truckin' are not modelled: Lazy's tab writes its solo grooves straight at 185 though the record is heard as a shuffle, and Pictures of Home's only human tab (Songsterr 6132, 2023) is unmarked and off the sixteenth grid in most bars. Read both against the records.
The one-handed roll (Bonedo names a video with Chad Smith): find and read the video for what it is and where he plays it on record.
Kit by year: Bonedo dates the Silver Sparkle Ludwig from about 1971 and Machine Head; when the big Ludwig with the 26-inch bass drum came in, and which kit is on Burn, are not dated here.

Which drummers name him as an influence in their own words: Wikipedia's list (Grohl, Phillips, Burr, Dee) cites sources that were not read; Lars Ulrich's Rock Hall speech praises him but does not call him an influence.
Black Night: Bonedo calls the groove a shuffle; the tab writes it straight. Measure the record's swing.
Grip: Wikipedia says matched; which matched grip (German, American, French) is not sourced, so the record leaves `grip` out.

identity.name: Ian Paice
home_scenes: The Maze and the Hamburg clubs (1966 to 1968)
identity.summary: Deep Purple's drummer from its first line-up in 1968, the only member in every line-up and on every record. A self-taught, left-handed player raised on big-band records and his father's dance band, he swung a hard rock band: 'big band music in a rock 'n' roll context'. Open hats under the riff, the kick on the beat and the backbeat behind it, and fills of fast single strokes: Hush, Speed King, Black Night, Fireball's two bass drums, Highway Star, Smoke on the Water, Burn, Perfect Strangers.

traditions.impact: His influences were 'mainstream and big band jazz', Buddy Rich above all: 'of all the big band drummers he stood out head and shoulders'. 'I'm playing big band music in a rock 'n' roll context. That inherent swing and feel harkens back to those days.'
He played along with his father, a pianist, in waltzes and quicksteps, and then in his father's dance band: 'a wee bit insipid, but it was a start'.

traditions.tradition: British beat and early rock and roll
traditions.impact: Bobby Elliott of the Hollies, Ringo Starr and Little Richard's drummer Charles Connor among his first influences; later Carmine Appice, Ginger Baker and Mitch Mitchell.

formative_events.event: A violin he could not play, turned over and hit: 'I flogged the violin and found a tom-tom and some old biscuits tins.' A £32 kit at 15.
The Maze (first called MI5), with Rod Evans, after Georgie and the Rave-Ons (later the Shindigs); the Maze played Hamburg, where Ritchie Blackmore saw him.
At 19, chosen on the spot to replace Bobby Woodman in the new Deep Purple; Hush, recorded in May, went to No. 4 in the US.
Self-taught: 'All my knowledge of rudiments is self taught and I have all the control I need.' 'If you can play singles right, everything else comes easy.'

eras.label: Mark I
eras.context: Rod Evans and Nick Simper: Shades of Deep Purple, The Book of Taliesyn, Deep Purple. Covers and organ-led psychedelic rock; Hush.
defining_traits: the snare on every beat for a chorus

eras.label: Mark II
eras.context: Ian Gillan and Roger Glover: In Rock, Fireball, Machine Head, Made in Japan, Who Do We Think We Are. The records that made the band, and hard rock.
defining_traits: the crash pushed onto the 'and' of 4
the ride in quarters under the solos
eras.style_shift: From an organ-led covers band to the loudest hard rock band of its day.

eras.label: Mark III and IV
eras.context: David Coverdale and Glenn Hughes: Burn, Stormbringer, then Come Taste the Band with Tommy Bolin. Funk and soul in the band; his drums 'strongly featured' on Burn.
defining_traits: sixteenths on the snare between the vocal lines

eras.label: Between Purples
eras.context: Paice Ashton Lord (1976 to 1978), Whitesnake (1979 to 1982), Gary Moore (1982 to 1984).

eras.label: The reunion and after
eras.context: Mark II again from Perfect Strangers (1984), then with Steve Morse and Don Airey, and Simon McBride; Pearl kits from 1982. The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Deep Purple in 2016.

genres.notes: What he says he plays in a rock context; not a genre he recorded in.

evidence.note: 'My bass drum is on the beat, or maybe even slightly ahead, but my backbeat—the snare drum—is behind it.' Not measured.

swing.notes: Straight eighths and sixteenths in every tab read; the swing he names is in the feel, not a triplet grid. Bonedo hears Black Night as a shuffle; the tab writes it straight.

dynamics.balance: A loud band, but the snare often played in the middle of the head rather than with a rimshot: 'sometimes you can play quieter in the middle of the head, which gives a much bigger impression'. Ghost notes in Smoke on the Water's verse and under its solo, few elsewhere.

feel_profile.interaction: The motor under Blackmore's riffs and Lord's organ ('he was the motor of the band'): the kick doubles the riff, the crash is pushed with it onto the 'and' of 4, and the hands fill the gaps in the vocal lines (Burn).

hand_techniques.name: Fast single strokes
hand_techniques.description: 'Extremely fast and smooth single and double-stroke rolls', self-taught; 'if you can play singles right, everything else comes easy'. Of Buddy Rich's single-stroke roll: 'I can do that roll at the same speed, but I can't keep it going anywhere near as long.'

hand_techniques.name: Sixteenths on the snare between the vocal lines
hand_techniques.description: Burn's verse: a groove bar and a bar of the snare in sixteenths, accents on the beat and the 'a', the kick on every beat, by turns; Smoke on the Water's guitar solo over the snare in sixteenths, an accent on each beat.

hand_techniques.name: Half-open hat closed by the foot
hand_techniques.description: Smoke on the Water's verse: the hat half open on the beats and closed by the foot on the 'and's.

hand_techniques.name: One-handed roll
hand_techniques.description: A one-handed roll on the snare, shown in a video with Chad Smith; how it is played is not described.

evidence.note: The video was not watched.

foot_techniques.name: One bass drum
foot_techniques.description: He prefers one bass drum (a 26-inch on stage), and plays on it what others use two for; a second bass drum for Fireball alone, set up for the encore.

rudiments.name: Triplets (single strokes in threes)
rudiments.application: 'Go on threes. Don't do Daddy Mammies - do Dad-Da-Da Mum-Ma-Ma.'

devices.description: Black Night's riff turns on two bars of quarter-note triplets, the kick and the hat by turns so that each plays six to the bar, three against each half bar, under the snare on 1 and 3.

evidence.note: Read from the human tab on a sextuplet grid (bars 5-6 and 9-10); not checked against another transcription.

searched: Songsterr human drum tabs (aiGenerated false), read section by section: Hush 6134, Speed King 5568, Black Night 23516, Fireball 29173, Highway Star 490, Smoke on the Water 329, Burn 6383, Perfect Strangers 22502; Lazy 5465 and Pictures of Home 6132 skimmed
Modern Drummer, Ken Micallef (2020); Rhythm, Chris Welch (c. 1995); Bonedo (2026)
Simon Poole, 'Speed King: Setting the Paice' (2025): the abstract only
Wikipedia: Ian Paice and the albums from Shades of Deep Purple to Perfect Strangers
devices_search.note: One device: Black Night's quarter-note triplets. Perfect Strangers' chorus alternates bars of 4/4 and 5/4, which is odd meter, not a device. Fireball's intro puts the snare in 3+3+2 eighths over the two bass drums inside one bar, a grouping of the riff with no cross pulse. Burn's sixteenths accent the beat and the 'a', inside the beat.

voice_language.snare: Backbeat on 2 and 4, often from the middle of the head; runs of sixteenths in fills and between vocal lines; ghosts in Smoke on the Water.
voice_language.kick: On the beat or ahead of it, doubling the riff; eighths on two bass drums in Fireball.
voice_language.toms: Fills high to floor in sixteenths; both toms in sixteenths under Hush's chorus.
voice_language.hihat: Open in quarters under the riff (Hush, Highway Star, Burn), open in eighths (Perfect Strangers), sixteenths in Smoke on the Water's intro, half-open on the beats in its verse.
voice_language.cymbals: The ride in quarters under the solos, its bell in Fireball; crashes pushed onto the 'and' of 4 and of 2; the second crash in quarters through Speed King. 'I want the cymbals to ring.'

aesthetic: a live corridor on Fireball and Machine Head
sound_profile.cymbal_character: Zildjian early, then Paiste from about 1971, the 2002 series his trademark: 'I want the cymbals to ring. I want this lovely natural decay of an acoustic instrument.'

by_era.description: A Ludwig in Black Oyster Pearl, 22-inch bass drum, Supraphonic snare; Pye Studios.
A Ludwig in Silver Sparkle; on Fireball and Machine Head the kit in a corridor, which sounded better to him than a studio.
Pearl from 1982, a 26-inch bass drum; a steel snare, 'very rock 'n' roll, immensely powerful'.

sample_hints.70s: Big, open Ludwig with a deep bass drum and long-ringing cymbals; a live room.

signature_traits.label: Big band in a rock band
signature_traits.description: 'I'm playing big band music in a rock 'n' roll context.' The kick on the beat or ahead of it, the backbeat behind: a push and pull he names himself.

signature_traits.label: Fast single strokes
signature_traits.description: Fills of single strokes on the snare and down the toms at tempos past 170 (Highway Star, Burn), from a self-taught player who measured himself against Buddy Rich's roll.

signature_traits.label: Open hats in quarters under the riff
signature_traits.description: The hat left open on each beat, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick with the riff: Hush, Highway Star's verse, Burn.

signature_traits.label: The crash pushed with the riff
signature_traits.description: The crash and kick on the 'and' of 4, tied over the bar line, bar after bar in Highway Star's chorus; then on the 'and' of 2 and of 4.

signature_traits.label: Fireball's two bass drums
signature_traits.description: Eighths on two bass drums at 240 under the ride's bell: 'a rare instance of Ian Paice playing a double-bass drum', and an early template for metal's double kick.

patterns.name: Hush: the groove
patterns.function: Open hats in quarters over a busy kick: 1, its 'and', the 'and' of 2, 3, the 'and' of 3 and the 'a' of 4

evidence.note: Songsterr's commonest bar (x25 under the organ solo, and the intro and verse).

patterns.name: Speed King: the verse
patterns.function: The second crash in quarters at 196, the kick on 1, its 'and', the 'and' of 2 and of 3

evidence.note: Songsterr verse bars 10, 11, 14 and 15, in eighths.

patterns.name: Black Night: the riff's turn in triplets
patterns.function: The kick and the hat by turns in quarter-note triplets, the snare on 1 and 3

evidence.note: Songsterr bar 5 (and 9), read at six steps a beat.

patterns.name: Fireball: the intro
patterns.function: Two bass drums in eighths at 240, the ride's bell in quarters, the snare in 3+3+2

evidence.note: Songsterr bars 2, 3 and 7, in eighths; which foot plays which eighth is not in the tab.

patterns.name: Highway Star: the verse
patterns.function: Open hats in quarters, the kick on 1, 3 and its 'and'

evidence.note: Songsterr verse bars 3, 5, 7, 11 and 15; bars 2, 6, 10 and 14 put the kick on the 'and' of 2 for 3.

patterns.name: Highway Star: the chorus push
patterns.function: The crash and kick on the 'and' of 4, tied over the bar line

evidence.note: Songsterr chorus bars 2, 3, 5 and 6.

patterns.name: Smoke on the Water: the verse
patterns.function: The hat half open on the beats, the foot closing it on the 'and's, ghosts on the 'a' of 2

evidence.note: Songsterr first verse, bars 6, 7 and 10 (every bar of the verse differs a little).

patterns.name: Smoke on the Water: under the solo
patterns.function: The snare in sixteenths, an accent on each beat, the kick in quarters, the hat foot on 2 and 4

evidence.note: Songsterr solo bars 3, 4, 6 and 7. The catalogue style plays it without the 'e', which its critic needs.

patterns.name: Burn: the roll between the lines
patterns.function: A bar of the snare in sixteenths, accents on the beat and the 'a', the kick on every beat, after each groove bar of the verse

evidence.note: Songsterr verse bar 14 (bars 1 and 16 are nearly the same).

patterns.name: Perfect Strangers: the chorus's bar of 5/4
patterns.function: Open hats in eighths for four beats, then the snare on 5 and two sixteenths on its 'and'

evidence.note: Songsterr bars 59, 61, 96, 98 and others, each after a bar of 4/4.

equipment.label: Ludwig in Black Oyster Pearl
equipment.layout_notes: A four-piece, later with an 18x16 floor tom. Left-handed: the kit mirrored.

evidence.note: Bonedo's account; the end year is inferred from its dating of the Silver Sparkle kit.

equipment.label: Ludwig in Silver Sparkle
equipment.layout_notes: Sizes like the Black Oyster kit (Bonedo); on Machine Head. At the California Jam (1974): one rack tom on the bass drum and two floor toms, on his left; white coated heads, chrome.

evidence.note: The end year is a guess.

equipment.label: Pearl (from 1982)
equipment.layout_notes: First an MLX in natural maple with a 26-inch bass drum; one bass drum, a double pedal on some songs. Remo heads.

affiliations.name: Deep Purple
affiliations.notes: The only member in every line-up (1968 to 1976, and from 1984).

evidence.note: 'I'm playing big band music in a rock 'n' roll context.'
'Buddy Rich was a big influence on me; of all the big band drummers he stood out head and shoulders.'
Bonedo ties the 26-inch bass drum to Appice.
Wikipedia's list; its source was not read.
Poole hears Fireball's double kick behind Phillips's on Sin After Sin (1977).
Deep Purple's first drummer, replaced in 1968 before the first record.
Deep Purple and Paice Ashton Lord.
'He's an incredible drummer. And he was the motor of the band.'
Deep Purple Mark III and IV, then Whitesnake (1979 to 1982).

philosophy.idea: Get the single strokes right and the rest follows; practise triplets with each hand, in threes.
Play to your strengths and relax: you play drums because it is fun, and hitting harder than you should loses the feel.
A drummer should be able to play along with any style, jazz, rock or orchestral.

innovations: Big-band swing and single-stroke fills in the first hard rock records
Fireball's double bass drum (1971), an early template for metal's
The only constant member of Deep Purple

cultural_references.description: Lars Ulrich, inducting Deep Purple into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (2016): 'little Ian Paice, a rock & roll cocktail of hair, sweat, spit and position'.
Rolling Stone placed him 21st among drummers (as Poole reports it).

common_misconceptions: That he plays two bass drums: one, but for Fireball.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A big 1970s rock kit, a deep bass drum and long-ringing cymbals
generation_rules: Straight time with the kick on the beat and the backbeat a little behind it.
Open hats in quarters under the riff; the ride in quarters under a solo.
The crash pushed onto the 'and' of 4 with the kick.
Fills of single strokes on the snare and down the toms, at phrase ends and between vocal lines.
avoid: Busy ghosted funk sixteenths as the main groove

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: His father's dance band, Krupa and Buddy Rich on record, the Hollies' Bobby Elliott and Ringo; then fifty-odd years behind Jon Lord and Ritchie Blackmore.
